no: Suppose that P = \(p : q : r\) (barycentyrics) is a point in the plane of a triangle ABC, and let A'B'C' be the cevian triangle of P. Let A'' be the point, other than P, of the interserction of the circumcircles of PBC' and PCB', and define B'' and C'' cyclically. Then A''B''C'' is perspective to ABC, and the perspector is the point \(f(P) = a^{2}(p + q)(p + r)\): \(b^{2}(q + r)\) (q + p) : \(c^{2}(r + p)\) (r + q).

Let "conj" abbreviate "conjugate"; then \(f(P) = complement of isotomic conj of cyclocevian conj of isotomic conj of P\) \(f(P) = complement of anticomplementary conj of P\) f(P) = isogonal conj of midpoint of X_2 and (reflection of P in X_2) f(P) = isogonal conj of midpoint of X_3 and (reflection of P in X_5) f(P) = isogonal conj of midpoint of X_4 and (reflection of P in X_3)
